# Semaglutide Effects on Cardiovascular Outcomes in People With Overweight or Obesity - SELECT
## Contribution To Literature:
The SELECT trial showed that in patients with overweight or obesity and established CVD but without diabetes, once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide was associated with a decreased risk of MACE comprised of CV death, nonfatal MI, and stroke compared with placebo.

answer:
A systematic review and meta-analysis found that semaglutide reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes [1]. Semaglutide modestly improved cardiovascular mortality, but did not significantly affect nonfatal stroke incidence [1].

The SELECT trial found that once-weekly semaglutide was associated with a 20% reduction in major adverse cardiac events over a mean 33 months [2]. This benefit occurred in patients with overweight or obesity and established cardiovascular disease without diabetes [2].
